claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.text:
## Child Benefit Eligibility Assessment Result

**I'm sorry, but you are NOT eligible for Child Benefit for Alex.**

### Why:

Alex is 18 years old, which falls into the 16-19 age category. For children in this age group, they must be in **approved education or training** to qualify as a "qualifying child" for Child Benefit purposes.

Since Alex is not currently in approved education or training, and is not in an extension period following recent education, he does not meet the qualifying criteria.

### Important Information:

**Child Benefit eligibility for 16-19 year olds requires:**
- The child must be in approved education or training, such as:
  - A-levels or Scottish Highers
  - NVQ Level 3 or below
  - Other approved non-advanced education courses

**OR**

- If a 16-17 year old has just left education, Child Benefit can continue for up to **20 weeks** if they register with the careers service or armed services (known as an "extension period")

### What happens now:

- If Alex was previously receiving Child Benefit and has recently left education, your benefit will stop
- Once a child reaches 20, Child Benefit stops regardless of their education status
- If Alex resumes approved education or training in the future while still under 20, you may be able to reclaim Child Benefit at that time

If you have any questions about what counts as "approved education" or need further guidance, you can contact the Child Benefit Office for more information.
